statement: The first line holds R and C. The next R lines each hold a string of C digits: 1 is land, 0 is water. An island is a maximal group of land cells connected 4-directionally - up, down, left, right; diagonal contact joins nothing. Print the number of islands. Scan every cell; each time unvisited land appears, count one island and flood it with a BFS or DFS using the four direction offsets as implicit edges.

example.why: The top-left block, the centre cell and the bottom-right pair are mutually unreachable.

hint: No adjacency list exists or is needed - the four offsets are the edges.
mistake: Treating diagonal neighbours as connected; under the 4-directional rule corners are strangers.
